subject: linear-algebra
subtopics: the definition Av = lambda v with v non-zero, and the geometric reading of an eigenvector as a direction the matrix only scales
the characteristic equation det(A - lambda I) = 0, its degree n, and its n roots over the complex numbers counted with multiplicity
the eigenspace null(A - lambda I) for a known eigenvalue, and computing eigenvectors by solving that homogeneous system
the identities sum of eigenvalues = trace and product of eigenvalues = determinant
eigenvalues of A^k, A^-1, A^T, cA, A + cI and polynomials p(A), with the eigenvectors left unchanged
algebraic against geometric multiplicity, the bound 1 <= GM <= AM, and what a shortfall means
diagonalisability, the criterion of n independent eigenvectors, A = P D P^-1 and the power shortcut
real symmetric matrices: real eigenvalues, orthogonal eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues, and AM = GM
complex eigenvalues of a real matrix: conjugate pairs, the discriminant test, and the absence of real eigenvectors
eigenvalue shortcuts for triangular, constant-row-sum, all-ones J, J - I and rank-one matrices
what preserves eigenvalues: similarity P^-1 A P and transposition, and the fact that elementary row operations do not
the Cayley-Hamilton theorem and the inverse obtained from it

chosen.channel: NPTEL, IIT Kharagpur (Prof. Jitendra Kumar, Engineering Mathematics I)
chosen.title: Lecture 46: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
covers: the definition with the vector non-zero, and the two readings of an eigenvector: parallel vectors, and non-trivial null vectors of A - lambda I
the characteristic equation of degree n and the reading of its roots as eigenvalues counted with multiplicity
the eigenspace as the null space of A - lambda I, including the zero vector
a worked 2x2 example with eigenvalues 3 and -2, and the repeated-root example whose double eigenvalue yields one eigenvector direction
the statement that distinct eigenvalues give linearly independent eigenvectors
Cayley-Hamilton and the inverse of a 2x2 obtained from it
chosen.why: The one source this run whose teaching could be read from beginning to end, and the only readable lecture that takes the topic from the definition through the characteristic equation and the eigenspace to Cayley-Hamilton in one pass, at exactly the level a beginner needs. Its worked examples were re-derived independently before being used, and its characteristic equation of the 2x2 example matches the values recomputed in scripts/validate.py. Read in full: the transcript text ran from the opening greeting to the closing references, so no part of the lecture is reconstructed from its title.

chosen.channel: NPTEL-NOC IIT Madras (Prof. Mitesh Khapra, CS7015 Deep Learning)
chosen.title: Lec 6.1 Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
covers: the 'what happens when a matrix hits a vector' framing, which is the clearest statement of the geometric idea found this run
eigenvectors as the vectors that refuse to leave their line, with the eigenvalue as the scale factor
the dominant eigenvalue defined by magnitude rather than sign
the two-restaurant transition matrix as a reason eigenvalues matter: repeated application of a matrix and the steady state
chosen.why: Chosen for the geometric intuition and for the one application that makes the topic feel motivated, not for the mechanics, which the NPTEL Kharagpur lecture covers better. It is a computer-science lecture, so the framing matches a GATE CSE reader. Read in part: the transcript text returned covered the opening through the stochastic-matrix and steady-state discussion; the later PCA and SVD sections of the lecture were not read.

chosen.title: Eigen Value Eigen Vector | Engineering Mathematics ONESHOT (Hindi)
covers: the characteristic equation of a 3x3 matrix written as lambda^3 - s1 lambda^2 + s2 lambda - det = 0, with s1 the trace and s2 the sum of the principal 2x2 minors
computing eigenvectors by Cramer's rule on A - lambda I, with the working shown for a 3x3 matrix
the repeated-eigenvalue case and how many eigenvectors to expect
the inverse of a 2x2 obtained from Cayley-Hamilton, worked on A = [[2,4],[3,5]]
chosen.why: Chosen deliberately so that this topic is not built from English sources alone, and it is the only non-English lecture whose transcript could be read this run. It is also the only readable source that gives the 3x3 characteristic polynomial in the principal-minor form, and its Cayley-Hamilton inverse example was re-derived independently before use. Every sentence taken from it is translated from Hindi into English and the cards say so. Read in part: the transcript covered the opening, the characteristic-equation and eigenvector methods, the repeated-eigenvalue discussion and the Cayley-Hamilton section; the closing practice questions were not read.

chosen.title: Linear Algebra subject notes and revision notes
covers: the algebraic multiplicity as the multiplicity of a root of det(A - lambda I) = 0, and the geometric multiplicity as the dimension of the eigenspace
the property list: sum of eigenvalues is the trace, product is the determinant, powers and inverses carry the eigenvalue to the same power and the reciprocal
the row-sum, rank-one and all-ones shortcuts used on the structured-matrix card
chosen.why: A GATE-oriented note set written for CSE readers, and the only readable English source that states the AM and GM definitions in the form the 2026 question needs. It is used for definitions and the property list only; every property is then re-derived and recomputed. Read in part: the fetched page body was cut off in the determinant section, so the eigenvalue notes were read through the search extract and the mark-distribution table, not end to end.

standard_refs: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra (eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalisation, powers of a matrix)
Lay, Linear Algebra and Its Applications (the characteristic equation, multiplicity, and the spectral theorem for symmetric matrices)
Hoffman and Kunze, Linear Algebra (eigenvalues, the characteristic polynomial, Cayley-Hamilton, and the real symmetric case)
Kolman and Hill, Elementary Linear Algebra with Applications (the 2x2 and 3x3 characteristic polynomial, and diagonalisation tests)
note: Every eigenvalue, eigenvector, multiplicity, trace, determinant and power published in this topic is recomputed by check_eigenvalues_and_eigenvectors() in scripts/validate.py, in exact rational arithmetic: the characteristic polynomial coefficients of each published matrix, the eigenpairs by A v = lambda v, the multiplicity pairs, the A^k and A^-1 and A^T relations, the symmetric orthogonality and entry-square identity over every small integer symmetric matrix, the Cayley-Hamilton identity over every small integer 2x2 matrix, and the row-operation counterexample. No source is quoted; each card paraphrases and then re-derives. The one non-English source is Hindi, read in part, and every sentence taken from it is translated and marked as translated on the cards that use it. The one English lecture that could be read end to end is recorded as FULL; every other source is PARTIAL or UNAVAILABLE and says exactly what was and was not read.
